cohort: The study included 583 women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and singleton pregnancies from the Lithuanian University of Health Sciences Birth Registry, divided into 202 obese women and 381 normal-weight women based on pre-pregnancy BMI.
finding: Obese women with GDM experienced significantly higher fasting glycaemia, a greater incidence of various pregnancy complications, and adverse neonatal outcomes like macrosomia and lower Apgar scores compared to normal-weight women with GDM.
mod_finding: Obese women with GDM had a higher incidence of induced labour and caesarean section (with more emergency caesarean sections) compared to normal-weight women with GDM.
